argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than the audit frames. It supports certification only as a caveated certification theory: current aggregate readiness passes, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the current legal-intake weakness is already identified as the material limitation that must control the certification basis. The actor is not claiming prior approval or informal monitoring cures the current gap; those items are context only. The supportable position is that certification is defensible only if treated as conditioned on explicit current-release disclosure of the legal-intake regression, not as an unqualified clean pass.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the compliance basis and should not decide the verdict. At most, it explains why a bounded caveat and no further escalation is the proportionate response if the auditor accepts the narrow certification theory rather than treating the record as an attempt to bypass policy.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not let aggregate readiness override a current material weakness, and it does not let prior approval or informal monitoring substitute for current evidence or approved mitigation. On this record, the only policy-consistent defense is narrow: certification can be defended, if at all, only on a caveated basis tied to the requirement that the current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and disclose the legal-intake regression for the named launch use case. The audit concern is correct that the present record does not show an attached disclosure artifact or approved mitigation artifact; that weakens the support level, but it does not justify reframing the actor's position as reliance on inadmissible substitutes.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence in this record showing the current release documentation itself or an approved risk-acceptance artifact.
The certification case is weak, not strong, because the disclosure-or-approved-mitigation predicate is unresolved in the packet.
Prior family approval and the informal monitoring comment cannot close the policy gap.
